lead: Boca Raton is full of condos, gated communities and seasonal homes. Leaks between units, AC drain overflows and tropical storms drive most of its water damage.
risk: condo leaks, AC drain overflows and tropical storm damage
why: Many Boca Raton residents live in condos and townhomes, and many are part-year residents. When a water heater, washing machine hose or AC drain fails in an empty unit, water can run for days and reach the units below. These losses often involve an association, several owners and several insurers. Quick drying and clear moisture records keep a one-unit leak from growing.

About 44% of homes were built before 1980, many with cast-iron drains and older supply lines. South Florida's long, wet summer keeps AC systems running nonstop, and clogged condensate lines overflow into ceilings and closets. Tropical storms bring wind-driven rain through roofs, windows and sliding doors. In the humidity, mold can start on wet drywall within a day or two.

image_caption: In Boca Raton condos, a leak in one unit can quickly reach the unit below.
problems: Downtown Boca, Spanish River, Por La Mar
Single-family homes in Boca Square, Camino Gardens
tips: Shut the water off before leaving for the season.
Clear the AC condensate line every few months.
Condo owners: keep your HO-6 and the association policy on file.
Replace washer and water heater hoses every five to seven years.
areas: Calls come from Downtown Boca, Royal Palm, Spanish River, Boca Square, Camino Gardens, the Golden Triangle, Por La Mar and Pearl City, plus Delray Beach, Highland Beach and Deerfield Beach.

faq.q: Who pays when a leak in a Boca Raton condo damages the unit below?
faq.a: It depends on the cause and your condo documents. Florida associations usually cover common elements, and owners cover their unit's interior and belongings under an HO-6 policy. The owner whose unit leaked may also be liable. Report it to management right away.
